newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CFOs see less robust fourth quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CFOs see less robust fourth quarter earnings.

text.p: U.S. chief financial officers are less optimistic for fourth quarter earnings growth, according to a recent survey.

About one-fourth of the participants indicated that third quarter earnings growth would not be sustained through the end of the year, the Financial Executives Institute/Duke-Fuqua School of Business Corporate Business Outlook survey said.
"These lowered expectations do not bode well for a year-end rally in the stock market," said Fuqua professor Michael Bradly, who co-directed the survey.

But chief financial officers were still strongly optimistic for the next 12 months, said Financial Executives Institute Chairman Frank Borelli, who is also senior vice president and chief financial officer of Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc.
The survey was conducted between October 1 and October 18, of 636 chief financial officers who were members of Financial Executives Institute.

As of October, 22 percent of financial executives surveyed expected the U.S. corporate earnings rate to decline in the fourth quarter, the survey said. But it found no signs of lower dividends, or decreased investment in capital equipment, research and development or merger and acquisition activity.

The survey's other director, Campbell Harvey, also said there were signs more companies would turn to long-term debt. "Lower earnings growth suggests that equity issues will be less likely and firms will be drawn to the fixed-income market," he said.
